title: Safety lattice for optimizer suggestion deployment and rollback choreography
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Optimize produces batching/caching configuration recommendations that materially reduce token cost but change live serving behavior. We need a deployable safety lattice that governs how suggestions are enacted automatically (or semi-automatically), how canaries are executed, and how safe/easy rollback occurs.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible canary policy format (JSON schema) that can be attached to any Optimize suggestion
Rollout controller implements staged percentage ramps and staged workload-sliced canaries (by customer, route, or region)
Telemetry-driven rollback triggers (SLO breaches, error rate regression, quality drift, >X% cost delta) enforced within the controller
Operator approval hook where suggested changes above configured thresholds require manual sign-off
Complete audit trail for any automatic apply or rollback action stored in audit logs and surfaced in Console
implementation_notes: Introduce a lightweight canary driver inside the rollout service that can spin up traffic slices by metadata (route/customer/region)
Leverage existing runtime metrics pipeline: token latency, tail L95, error rate, and quality metrics from eval harness
Use simulation mode to run 'dry' applies against a shadowed traffic stream for at least one hour before any live canary
Store suggestion metadata + decision tree in the central config store (DB row per suggestion) for durable audit and rollback
Expose operations endpoints for immediate emergency rollback and for scheduled rollbacks with reason codes
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Simulation -- apply suggestion in simulation to representative traffic (1h) and surface predicted cost/latency delta
Phase 1: Canary-1 -- 1% traffic slice for 30m; require no SLO regressions and cost improvement within expected band
Phase 2: Canary-2 -- 10% traffic slice for 2h; run quality checks and compare embedding similarity / reranking metrics
Phase 3: Ramp -- linear ramp to 100% over configurable window (default 6h) with continuous monitoring
Phase 4: Post-rollout watch -- 24h elevated telemetry retention and automated revert if any trigger fires
canary_policy_spec: Default checks: latency_tail_ms (L95), error_rate, token_cost_delta, quality_delta (custom eval)
Slice selectors: route_id, customer_id, region, model_variant
Operator thresholds: SLO breach threshold (e.g., 1.2x baseline L95), error spike (>0.5%), cost overrun (>15% unexpected)
monitoring_and_telemetry: Link rollout events to per-token cost telemetry so we can attribute cost delta to the specific suggestion
Emit structured rollout events: {suggestion_id, phase, slice, metric_snapshot} to observability topic
Add Circuit Breaker metric that increments on each trigger and surfaces in Console with suggested remedies
Integrate with tracing to attribute tail-latency regressions to specific model or kernel decisions
rollback_triggers: Immediate: >=2x baseline error_rate or explicit 5xx spike for 1 minute
Near-term: L95 latency > 1.5x baseline sustained for 10 minutes
Quality: automatic eval shows quality_delta worse than configured threshold (e.g., >2% regression on holdout prompts)
Cost anomaly: observed token cost increases beyond predicted improvement band by >25%
Manual operator request with reason code: emergency_security, customer_outage, performance_regression
audit_and_approval_workflow: Suggestions tagged with 'high-impact' (config change >X tokens/sec or cost >Y) route to manual approval queue
Approvals captured with approver id, timestamp, and attestation text; stored in long-term audit store
Approval policy: single approver for low-impact, two approvers (PM + Eng) for high-impact, and SecOps sign-off when security_review_required=true
Automated emails and Console notifications for pending approvals; approval window expires after 72h
Post-action report generated and attached to suggestion: metrics, traces, and canary logs

2025-02-25 | Liam Chen: Prototyped slice selector using route_id + customer_tier; initial tests show stable slices for enterprise customers.

2025-03-01 | Asha Kapoor: Implemented minimal canary driver and simulated apply pipeline; hitting an intermittent race where two suggestions target same committer key — adding optimistic lock
2025-03-04 | Design (Evan Park): UX note — Console should show predicted cost delta and link to the eval sample set used for quality checks
decision_log: Use staged ramp + workload-sliced canaries rather than instant global flips to reduce blast radius
Require human approval for suggestions marked 'high-impact' by the estimator module
Simulate before canary as a hard requirement for all autosuggests to reduce false positives
Default rollback policy is automatic on trigger with operator notification; operator can opt to pause automatic rollback per suggestion

Add schema validation tests for canary_policy_spec and wire into CI
Schedule a runbook review with SRE and SecOps (target 2025-03-12)
